ch39.d.pot: Shape of the potential energy $U(x)$ that traps the electron
ch39.d.show: Draw the wave function $\psi_n$ or the probability density $|\psi_n|^2$ on each level
ch39.d.L: Width $L$ of the well (of each well for the double well)
ch39.d.U0: Potential energy $U_0$ outside the well (bottom of the well = 0)
ch39.d.hw: Level spacing $\hbar\omega$ set by the oscillator frequency $\omega$
ch39.d.Ub: Potential energy of the barrier between the two wells
ch39.d.b: Width of the barrier between the two wells
ch39.d.pair: The two stationary states mixed in equal parts, named by their quantum numbers $n$ (the oscillator starts at $n = 0$)
ch39.w.goal.quant: A confined particle can have only discrete energies (quantization)
ch39.w.goal.shape: The levels and wave functions are set by the shape of the potential
ch39.w.obs.inf: Infinite well: $E_n \propto n^2$; a narrower well spreads the levels apart ($\propto 1/L^2$)
ch39.w.obs.fin: Finite well: the wave function leaks past the walls and decays exponentially (classically forbidden region, dotted); there are finitely many bound states, more for a deeper well
ch39.w.obs.harm: Harmonic: all levels are spaced by $\hbar\omega$, and the lowest energy is $\hbar\omega/2$, not 0 (compare Ch 15)
ch39.w.obs.double: Double well: levels come in close pairs (symmetric and antisymmetric states); a thinner or lower barrier splits each pair more (the Σ panel gives each splitting $\Delta E$ directly), the starting point of bands in Ch 41
ch39.w.obs.nodes: State $n$ has $n - 1$ nodes; higher energy means shorter wavelength
ch39.s.goal.osc: Mixing two stationary states of different energy makes the probability density oscillate
ch39.s.goal.period: The period is $T = h/(E_b - E_a)$: a larger energy difference oscillates faster
ch39.s.obs.slosh: 1 + 2 (oscillator: 0 + 1): the density sloshes from side to side and $\langle x\rangle$ oscillates
ch39.s.obs.parity: 1 + 3 (oscillator: 0 + 2) in a symmetric potential: both states have the same symmetry, so $\langle x\rangle$ stays at 0 while the shape breathes
ch39.s.obs.tunnel: Double well 1 + 2: the particle tunnels back and forth through the barrier; a smaller pair splitting gives a longer period
ch39.assume.electron: Particle: an electron ($m = m_e$) in one dimension
ch39.assume.fd: Solution method: the finite well uses the exact solution (roots of the transcendental equations, exponential decay outside). The infinite, harmonic and double wells are solved numerically by finite differences (1500–2400 grid points); the harmonic potential has hard walls at ±7 nm (outside the plotted range), and the outer vertical lines of the double well are hard walls
ch39.assume.amp: Wave-function heights are in arbitrary units (every state drawn the same height); the baseline sits at the state's energy; the close pairs of the double well overlap on almost the same baseline (upper state dashed)
ch39.assume.supamp: Density height in arbitrary units; baseline at the mean energy $(E_a + E_b)/2$
ch39.s.assume.range: Ranges in this tab: well width at least 1.0 nm, finite-well depth at least 1.8 eV, so every potential holds three or more bound states and all three pairs exist
ch39.s.assume.terms: Stationary state: a state $\psi_n(x)$ of definite energy; its probability density does not change in time. $\psi$ is the spatial part, $\Psi(x,t)$ the full wave function including time
ch39.s.assume.mean: $\langle x\rangle = \int x\,|\Psi|^2\,dx$: the expectation value of position (mean position), the average of many measurements on the same state. Blue dot and the plot below
ch39.s.assume.time: The period ranges from 1.4 fs (infinite well, 1 + 3) to about 13 000 fs (double well, high and wide barrier), so the plot shows the last 3 periods and at 1× one period takes 2 s. $\Delta E$ is the gap between the two levels (in the double well $E_1$ and $E_2$ look equal at the printed precision)
